p.em: Fifteen terms. Everything else on the hub is ordinary English.

tr.td: The website. Four areas along the top: Discover, My workspace, Build, Learn.
The shared toolbox of reusable AI building blocks, called components. The hub lists every one of them.
One building block in one of six kinds: an agent, a harness, a tool, an integration, a pattern, or a skill.
Where a component is once two named people have signed it. "On the shelf" means "safe to reuse".
A named person's word that they tested and read a component. Two are needed: its owner, and an AI security engineer.
One of six approved ways to build something, R1 to R6. Picking a road decides which checks apply.
How much an action can change. GreyR reads. YellowW1 writes after you confirm. RedW2 needs a second person. PurpleMONEY is refused.
How much autonomy a person or a service is allowed, L0 to L3. A service never acts above the person using it.
The one-page form that starts any new use of AI. Six sections, about fifteen minutes.
Something you talk to that reads pages and answers with the page named. It has no tools, so it cannot change anything.
Something that can read real systems and propose an action. A write waits for you; money is refused.

The loop an agent runs inside. It checks every call the same way; the model cannot skip it. Any brief that names a tool carries it automatically, with the guard, the engine, the chain and ids-only logging.
The separate site of practice pages. Every component has a page there too.
One engineer per team who carries one initiative and brings the result back to the collection.
The spark button at the bottom right of every page. It walks you through the hub and answers from our own pages.
